newsitem.title: FINLAND: Thin Helsinki up, cheered by early US techs rally.
newsitem.headline: Thin Helsinki up, cheered by early US techs rally.

text.p: Shares ended up after dozing at higher levels most session on Friday, and a continued rally in tech stocks early on Wall Street and dollar strength against the markka cheered the outlook, brokers said.

The technology-laden Nasdaq index in the U.S. rose 0.6 percent in early dealings and Nokia joined the spurt to close up 2.00 markka or 0.7 percent at 299.00 markka, accounting for almost a third of thin volume.
The HEX general index closed up 0.59 percent at 2,823.83 after trading in a tight 2,813.06-2,826.92 range. The FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark rose 0.77 percent to 986.64.
Compared to last Friday, the HEX was up 0.43 percent.
The tech sector in the U.S. was cheered by higher- than-forecast Q3 earnings at Microsoft.
Forestries were helped by strength overseas: UPM-Kymmene continued to lead on hopes that it would announce purchasing healthy parts of troubled Canadian paper group Repap.
UPM closed up 1.30 markka at its 114.50 markka session high and the forestry index was up 0.83 percent.
"There is fundamental demand for forestries, they will show gains again next week," one broker predicted.
Other cyclicals could also be strong, brokers said.
"All conditions favour buying cyclicals at the moment," said one, pointing to the stronger dollar. USD/FIM fell to 5.1705 as Helsinki treasury markets closed from 5.1845 on Thursday.
"We could see some money flowing into stocks again next week as interest rates in the U.S. and at home seem to be steadying," said another.

Interest in wholesaler Kesko was boosted by the EU's approval of the partial unwinding of its merger with Tuko, which brokers said cleared the air. Trade was brisk for Kesko at 19 million markka but gains modest, 1.20 markka to 71.70.
